title: personal-llm-experiment-mini-sheet
content:
Mini experiment tracker (personal) - quick table for recent inference tuning runs

Columns: experiment_id, date, model, variant, prompt_template, temp, top_p, quant (bits), batch_size, seq_len, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, throughput_tok_s, cost_per_1k_tok_usd, eval_set, rouge_l, exact_match, notes

Rows:
EXP-2026-01A, 2026-01-05, mpt-7b, fp16, simple-system+user, 0.0, 0.9, none, 8, 256, 23, 78, 1200, 0.045, convo-eval-v1, 0.34, 0.21, baseline for convo prompts
EXP-2026-01B, 2026-01-08, mpt-7b, int8, simple-system+user, 0.0, 0.9, int8, 8, 256, 28, 95, 950, 0.032, convo-eval-v1, 0.33, 0.20, ~25% cost saving, slight latency bump
EXP-2026-01C, 2026-01-15, llama2-13b, q4, metadata-context, 0.0, 0.95, q4, 4, 512, 45, 120, 700, 0.065, summarization-set-v2, 0.52, 0.44, better summaries but higher cost
EXP-2026-01D, 2026-01-20, gptx-3b-erm, fp16, instr-follow-v2, 0.1, 0.8, none, 16, 128, 18, 42, 1500, 0.030, terse-qna, 0.28, 0.19, good throughput for short queries
EXP-2026-02E, 2026-02-12, mpt-7b, fp16, prefix-cache-enabled, 0.0, 0.9, none, 8, 512, 21, 60, 1300, 0.047, convo-eval-v1, 0.36, 0.22, enabled kv-prefix cache -> p95 improved on repeated prefixes

Quick notes and observations:
- int8/integer quant reduces cost ~25-30% on mpt-7b variant; small decrease in rouge/em but acceptable for some routes.
- q4 (llama2-13b) gives good quality uplift for long-context summarization but costs ~35% more than fp16 mpt; consider targeted routing for high-value long docs.
- Batch size tuning: for short queries (seq_len <= 128) increasing batch_size to 16 gave best throughput without p95 degradation; for long-context, smaller batches keep p95 in control.
- Prefix/KV cache drastically reduces p95 for repeated conversational prefixes (see EXP-2026-02E). Worth integrating cache-hit metric into dashboard.

- [ ] Draft short note for team on recommended default profiles for internal apps (Riley to review).

- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/402 (kernel selector telemetry)
- Slack thread: slack://channel/CL4B2X3/thread/163847 (kv-cache perf discussion)

Scratchpad (ideas to test next):
- Adaptive temperature per-route based on historical score drop: lower temp for high-value outputs; test temp=0.0 vs 0.1 delta on rouge/em.
- Try micro-batching + pipeline concurrency to get better GPU utilization for 1k-3k token requests.
- Quick script: export last 30 runs -> csv -> upload to shared_confluence as baseline table.

Notes to self: keep this mini-sheet lightweight (one-page), move cleaned/aggregated results to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/experiment-logs when ready for wider consumption.

End of mini-sheet.
